comparator.name: Business Analytics
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC: ten 6-EC first-year courses, ten 6-EC second-year courses, and a third year comprising 30 EC of genuine free-choice study plus three 6-EC courses and a 12-EC Bachelor’s Thesis and Thesis Seminar. The programme integrates analytics, business economics and computer science through mathematics, probability and statistics, programming, AI and machine learning, operations research, econometrics, management applications and data projects. There is no formal specialisation route to select. The 30-EC free-choice semester is preserved as open rather than filled with invented content, and the explicitly credit-bearing 12-EC thesis component is retained as the research component.

alternatives.label: Business analytics across mathematics, data and organizations
alternatives.concept: Combines mathematical and statistical methods, programming, data science and AI with economic and business decisions. It approximates UvA’s integrated field through UCR courses while lacking its continuous specialist projects and full operations-research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has substantial quantitative, computational and business study; no one strand alone defines it.
progression: Verified against the GitHub enriched UCR workbook: each course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, all formal prerequisites are earlier, and mathematics/programming foundations precede advanced work where possible.

alternatives.label: Algorithms, AI and mathematical optimization
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on formal and computational methods for business-related decisions, with deeper software development, systems mathematics and reinforcement learning. Business foundations remain as the application setting, while the curriculum gives less room to marketing and organizational study.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced computing, mathematics and AI occupy the curricular differences from the integrated route.
alternatives.distinctness: Four course choices replace business AI, consumer engagement, market research and one advanced algorithms course with software development, linear systems, advanced calculus and reinforcement learning; the remaining technical courses still form a methodological concentration.
progression: Verified against the GitHub enriched UCR workbook: each course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, all formal prerequisites are earlier, and mathematics/programming foundations precede advanced work where possible.

alternatives.label: Data-informed markets, finance and strategy
alternatives.concept: Uses quantitative and data foundations to study prediction, customer analytics, finance and digital business strategy. It gives organizational applications greater weight than the integrated route and does not claim the UvA depth in optimization or advanced software.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set has a substantive business and market sequence supported by data and quantitative methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change from the integrated route: consumer economics, international business governance, applied finance and digital strategy replace advanced AI optimization, computational methods and algorithms. It differs even more strongly from the technical route.
progression: Verified against the GitHub enriched UCR workbook: each course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term, all formal prerequisites are earlier, and mathematics/programming foundations precede advanced work where possible.

selection.assessment: The integrated mathematics–computing–business curriculum is the closest feasible UCR response. A deeper algorithmic route and a predictive market-analytics route are separately evidenced and differ from each other and from the first route by at least four courses. Responsible organizational AI is recorded as a further target-specific direction, but the three-alternative maximum is reached.

notes.text: UvA Business Analytics requires a substantial sequence in calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, operations research, programming, machine learning and applied business analytics, including a 12-EC thesis and seminar; its third-year 30 EC free-choice semester remains open. UCR combines related quantitative, computing and business courses, but does not reproduce that full specialist sequence or the UvA project structure.
